description: Two changed files, defect in the SECOND one: transform_value's unknown-transform branch now returns the raw string instead of raising, so a caller that asked for "json" and mistyped the transform name silently receives a str where it expected a dict. The first file (cache.py) carries a genuinely innocent readability change, so the model must attribute its finding to the right file as well as the right line. This is the shape no other scenario has: every existing line_in scenario is single-FILE, so nothing exercises diff_map.walk_diff's per-file hunk attribution end to end. The PR body frames the defect as deliberate backwards-compatibility, so the model has to judge the change rather than accept the author's rationale.
line_accuracy_note: Exact line 31: `return value`, the swallowed unknown-transform error. The two files' reviewable ranges are deliberately DISJOINT (cache.py 16-23, transform.py 26-31) so a file-attribution slip fails provenance loudly instead of posting a comment on the wrong file at a coincidentally-valid line. artifact.annotate_diff resets its numbering per file; if this scenario starts failing on the path rather than the line, suspect diff_map.walk_diff's file tracking -- do NOT widen line_in.
